subject: Sizing playbook — three GPU options, streaming SLOs, pilot plan
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@edgemed.ai>, Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@edgemed.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: sizing playbook & GPU tradeoffs (streaming SLOs)

Hi Amit / Sophie — thanks for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment heading into a perf pilot. Low verbosity; action items at the bottom.

Call recap (as I heard it)
- Primary SLOs: streaming partials delivered as chunks with chunk latency <= 120ms (P95), final response P95 <= 250ms for ~256-token outputs.
- Traffic profile: steady state ~120 rps, mean request size ~65 tokens, average session concurrency ~130.
- Burst profile: short bursts up to ~350 rps for 20–45s during peak times.
- Quality: must keep model outputs at current fidelity (no heavy quantization that drops entity extraction precision).
- Platform requirements: server-sent-event streaming, per-request routing by region, and token-level cost visibility.

Sizing / GPU tradeoff summary (three options)
1) NVIDIA H100 80GB (recommended for latency-first)
   - Expected reserved throughput per GPU: ~900–1,100 tokens/sec (fp16/bf16 path) depending on prompt shape
   - Concurrency fit: 80–120 streaming sessions with low jitter; best P95 latency headroom
   - Cost: highest; fewer GPUs needed (starting slab: 3–4)
2) NVIDIA A100 80GB (balanced latency / cost)
   - Expected reserved throughput per GPU: ~550–750 tokens/sec
   - Concurrency fit: 40–80 streaming sessions; moderate P95 latency
   - Cost: mid; starting slab: 6–8 GPUs for your steady-state and burst buffer
3) NVIDIA L4 / T4 class (quantized, cost-optimized)
   - Expected reserved throughput per GPU: ~200–350 tokens/sec (with int8/4-bit quantization and reduced precision kernels)
   - Concurrency fit: high session count if you accept higher per-request latency and some quality risk
   - Cost: lowest; starting slab: 12–18 units (pilot will determine exact fit)

Operational notes
- Prefetch / KV cache: your conversational flows reuse prefixes frequently. We recommend enabling prefix KV caching on any dedicated deployment to reduce per-token compute.
- Batching: Redwood can perform continuous batching; for streaming we keep batch windows tight (~10–15ms) to meet chunk latency.
- Fallbacks: propose fallback routing to lower-cost variants during prolonged bursts to avoid OOM/queueing.

Pilot proposal (two-week closed pilot)
- Week 1: baseline benchmarks (synthetic workload using your prompt set + small sample of production traffic you can share). Redwood runs comparative runs on H100 / A100 / L4 with identical prompts and trace capture.
- Week 2: shadow traffic run (your real traffic mirrored at X% with monitoring), validate P95/P99 latency, per-token cost, and model quality regression tests (we’ll run your eval prompts).
- Deliverables: SLO heatmap, recommended reserved slab (GPU counts by type), cost estimate, and a short runbook for our ops team.

Asks from EdgeMed
- Can you share a 24–72h sample of production request traces (anonymized) + 20 representative prompts (edgemed-prompt-set.csv attached)?
- Confirm whether 120 rps steady / 350 rps burst are accurate or if we should plan larger headroom.

Next steps / owners
- Amit: share prompt set + 24–72h trace (attachment).
- Ben (cc): run three-way bench (H100 / A100 / L4) and share preliminary numbers by EOD Fri.
- Karthik (cc): review SLO gating criteria and confirm concurrency math for reserved slabs.
- Chloe: schedule kickoff + send mutual action plan (I’ll propose Wed morning).

Attachments: edgemed-prompt-set.csv, target-SLO-matrix.xlsx, pilot-scope.md

Thanks — chloe

--

From: Amit Shah <amit@edgemed.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: sizing playbook & GPU tradeoffs (streaming SLOs)

Chloe — thanks for the crisp recap. Confirming a few points:
- Steady-state is closer to 115–130 rps depending on the campaign; peak bursts have reached ~360 rps in our stress windows (so plan for 400rps headroom).
- Concurrency: our active sessions currently average 125, spiking to ~420 when several doctors are using the assistant simultaneously.
- We can share the anonymized traces (I’ll drop a 48h window to your Drive link).

Two quick asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood include a P99 tail estimate in the bench runs? We care about P95 for UX but P99 for SLA penalties.
2) For the L4 path: we need a short quality check for entity extraction—if int8 causes regressions we’d prefer the A100 path.

I’ll upload the traces and a short CSV of 20 canonical prompts to the Drive link today. Looking forward to Ben’s numbers.

— Amit

Looping in a few bench-level notes + proposed experiment matrix.

Quick notes:
- We will bench using your prompt set at three shape profiles: short (<=40 tokens), median (~65 tokens), long (~300 tokens). For streaming we’ll capture chunk delivery latencies at 32/64 token chunk sizes.
- P95 and P99 measured both at chunk delivery and final-response completion. We’ll report token/sec, per-request CPU/GPU utilization, and mem headroom.
- For L4 runs we’ll try int8 and 4-bit quantized builds; we’ll run the entity-extraction eval you mentioned and include a small confusion matrix.

Experiment matrix (high level)
- H100 x 3: baseline latency, warm KV cache, no quantization
- A100 x 6: balanced run with typical batching parameters
- L4 x 12: int8 and q4_0 runs, measure quality dropoff

Cost & ops note: initial cost delta (very rough): H100 slab (3) ~ 3x A100 slab (8) ~ 0.5x L4 slab (15) in monthly committed cost — will refine after bench.

Request to Amit / EdgeMed: if you can confirm a 48h trace and preferred evaluation prompts we’ll aim to have initial bench numbers by Fri EOD (Jun 4). If traces land late Thurs we’ll extend to Mon.

Ben

Thanks all — quick mutual-action-plan and calendar items below.

Mutual action plan (short)
- EdgeMed: upload 48h anonymized trace + canonical prompt CSV to shared Drive (Amit) — due: Fri EOD (Jun 5).
- Redwood (Ben): run three-way benchmark (H100/A100/L4) and post initial numbers to Drive + short SLO heatmap — due: Mon Jun 7 EOD.
- Redwood (Karthik): produce reserved-slab recommendation + runbook for ops (include autoscale thresholds and fallback mapping) — due: Tue Jun 8 midday.
- EdgeMed: review heatmap and confirm which GPU path to pilot — due: Wed Jun 9.

Kickoff meeting: I’ve proposed a 30-min kickoff for Mon Jun 7 9:30am PT — invite sent to all.

Deliverables & success criteria
- Deliverable: bench report with P95/P99 chunk and final response latencies, per-token cost, and basic quality regression notes.
- Success: chosen slab meets streaming chunk P95 <= 120ms and final-response P95 <= 250ms at steady-state traffic, with acceptable P99 tail for SLA.

If that all sounds correct I’ll lock in the kickoff and Ben will start the bench once traces arrive.

Best — chloe
